title: Annotatio II §.VI close: Union similitudes; Asceliniana egg-to-egg with modern Lutheran; stop before §.VII
pass_a_gloss: He adds similitudes for illustration of the Union of two Substances, not likewise for illustration of the Mode of Union: that we ourselves, he says, are compacted of corporeal and incorporeal, of mortal and immortal substance; and in Christ divine and human nature meet in one person. See this Letter to Berengar in Dacherius’s notes on the life of Lanfranc pp. 24–25 (Paris 1648), cited by Otrokocsi in the Irenicum pp. 79–80. These Ascelinian [sayings], especially since they promiscuously inculcate the Union of bread and Christ’s body without any distinction of regard to the pious and the impious, are as genuine to the modern Lutheran sentence as Egg to Egg.
pass_b_english: Similitudes illustrate the union of two substances, not the mode: we are compacted of corporeal/incorporeal and mortal/immortal; in Christ divine and human meet in one person.
Letter at Dacherius on Lanfranc (Paris 1648); Otrokocsi cites it.
These Asceliniana — union of bread and body without pious/impious distinction — match modern Lutheran sentence as egg to egg.
source_text: Addit, pro illustratione Unionis duarum Substantiarum, non item, pro illustratione Modi Unionis, Similitudines: quòd & nos ipsi, inquit, ex corporea & incorporea, ex mortali & immortali substantia sumus compacti; & in Christo divina humanaque natura convenit in unam personam. Vide hanc Epistolam ad Berengarium apud Dacherium in notis ad vitam Lanfranci pag. 24. & 25. Edit. Paris. anno 1648. allegante Otrokocsi in Irenico pag. 79. & 80. Hæc Asceliniana, praesertim cùm Unionem panis & corporis Christi promiscuè inculcent, citra omne discrimen respectûs ad pios & impios, tam genuina sunt modernæ sententiae Lutheranae, quàm Ovum Ovo.

lemmas.gloss: without distinction of pious and impious
